title: ContourGlobal secures 623 MWh of battery storage in Italy's second MACSE auction - ContourGlobal

body_markdown:
Rome, November 25, 2026


**ContourGlobal has been awarded 104 MW / 623 MWh of new battery storage capacity in the South and Calabria market area** . The award came in the second competitive auction of MACSE, Italy’s centralized mechanism for procuring electricity storage, run by grid operator Terna.


The auction awarded 16 GWh of new lithium-ion storage capacity across four market areas in Southern Italy and the islands, covering 100% of the required volume. Of this, the largest share went to the South and Calabria area, which obtained 9.6 GWh, or 60% of the total. It was in this competitive market area, more specifically in the Apulia region, that ContourGlobal was awarded a six-hour battery storage project, which will start construction next year and is expected to enter commercial operation ahead of the mandatory 2029 delivery date set in the auction terms.


The competitiveness of this auction was confirmed by bids totaling almost three times the capacity on offer. According to Terna, around 67 GWh of new projects qualified, and about 43 GWh were bid. The weighted average clearing price was €11,382/MWh-year, well below the €27,000/MWh-year reserve price and 12% lower than in the first MACSE auction (delivery 2028).


**How MACSE works.**


MACSE is a first-of-its-kind mechanism for the centralized procurement of utility-scale storage. Winners of Terna’s competitive auctions receive a fixed annual premium. In return, they build the storage systems and make their capacity available to the grid.


Terna then pools the capacity of all MACSE batteries and sells its use through time-shifting contracts, on a platform operated by Italy’s power exchange GME. These contracts are open to any producer or trader. Through them, renewable generators can move their solar and wind output to the hours of highest demand without owning a battery themselves. Capacity not sold for time-shifting is offered on the balancing and ancillary services market. The revenues from these products go towards covering the cost of the premium.


**Why it matters.**


Italy is already one of Europe’s storage leaders, with almost a fifth of the EU’s operating battery capacity at the end of 2025, and storage is becoming central to the country’s power system. Batteries charge when renewable energy is abundant and cheap and release it during the evening peak, when prices are highest and gas-fired plants usually set the price. Terna sizes MACSE volumes so that the cost of new storage stays below the savings from burning less gas.


“ *We are very proud of the success of our Italian team in a highly competitive tender where we demonstrated our commitment to Italy’s energy market. Storage and renewables must grow together in Italy: batteries make clean energy available when it is needed most and reduce the system’s exposure to gas prices. Storing solar and wind power in batteries to use in peak moments can cost up to 49% less than gas-fired generation, so these investments are key to energy affordability and energy security. MACSE is just one of the pieces of our complex BESS strategy, which includes long-term tolling agreements and merchant opportunities* ,” said **Antonio Cammisecra, CEO of ContourGlobal** .
